name: Brask Ford works
role: Ball and control valves, machining and pressure test
cells: Bar-stock machining :: 86 :: two shifts, third shift Mon–Thu||Ball grinding and lapping :: 72 :: ||Control valve trim :: 91 :: running hot, 11-week lead||Assembly and hydrotest :: 78 :: ||Sanitary finishing :: 64 ::
status_note: Control valve trim is running hot: lead time 11 weeks
summary: Our original plant, where every ball and control valve is machined, assembled and pressure tested.
body:
Brask Ford opened in 1957 (story) as a machine shop making brass gate valves. Today it runs twenty-two CNC machining centers, a ball lapping line and four hydrotest benches.

Every valve that leaves the plant has a test record tied to its serial number. Customers and distributors can request it with the serial number on the tag.

summary: Pumps, actuators and butterfly valves, with three pump test loops.
body:
Linnmoor opened in 2004 (story). Every pump runs on one of three test loops before it ships, and the curve is archived with the serial number.

Stock actuator sizes are built to order and usually ship the same week.
